findings.text: promotion_in_flight is consulted only when the live pointer is already absent, but a promotion holds its lease from reckon/crew/promotion.py:460 and removes the pointer only at reckon/crew/promotion.py:1414, so a resume issued during the whole promotion window finds the pointer present, takes a hold and launches — the race the section exists to close — and the done_when case that would have caught it is absent.

the MCP resume door calls resumption._resume directly and never passes the CLI guard installed at reckon/cli.py:670, so an MCP resume of a promoted run still ends silently and one of a delivered run takes no hold.
a new module named resume.py beside the existing resumption.py leaves two files whose names differ only by suffix and both own resume behaviour, and the plan's write path named resumption.py.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from 55d49260706d to f9eab85d420b; the feature commit adds resume.py (331 lines), three call-site edits and a 388-line test, and the two documentation commits add only the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names five cases; tests/test_a_coordinator_holds_a_delivered_run.py contains four of them (held-run deferral, recorded hold and release, promoted-run refusal naming its commit, hold-before-relaunch) and no case for a resume issued while a promotion is in flight, so one named case is unasserted.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is a coordinator hold over a delivered run plus a resume that never vanishes; reckon/crew/resume.py:57 hold_delivery writes it, reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:1920 skips a held run, reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:504 refuses it, and the hold, release and promoted-run refusal are all landed, but the "being promoted" refusal at reckon/crew/resume.py:219 is reached only once the pointer is already gone.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits f39a6fa1e2aba68b5e1437770dafdfa001707eef, c536fe6d9b, f9eab85d42; it records the head arm at 56 passed EXIT=0, the base arm at 49 passed 2 errors EXIT=1 attributed to scaffolding, the two importer arms, and the red negative control.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the source run's manifest orientation paths; every path in the diff is inside the granted set, and the plan's own list named resumption.py/crew_run_commands.py instead, recorded under evidence_inputs and outside_scope.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_coordinator_holds_a_delivered_run.py:196 and :262 fail if the lander or the resume hold is removed (shown by the 2-failed negative control), but the promotion_in_flight branch at reckon/crew/resume.py:159 has no assertion, so the missing case and its code are both unguarded.
justifications.evidence: the after-arm log records 56 passed EXIT=0 at f9eab85d and the two importer arms carry 12 identical failure/error identities, but the done_when's in-flight case is measured nowhere.
justifications.fit: the module follows the surrounding docstring-and-CrewError idiom, but reckon/crew/resume.py sits beside the existing reckon/crew/resumption.py and both names claim resume.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the hold and its two automatic doors work, but reckon/crew/resume.py:219 tests promotion_in_flight only when the live pointer is already absent, so the "being promoted" half of the goal is unmet.
justifications.reuse: the change reuses recovery.classify_pointer, pending_landing._promoted_row and runs._mutate_pointer instead of forking them; a search of reckon/crew for an existing landing-hold (queue_hold, budget_hold, pending_landing) found none.
justifications.scope_discipline: all six landed paths sit inside the dispatch-granted set in the source manifest, with the resumption.py deviation disclosed under outside_scope rather than taken silently.
